subject: Private deployment pricing sensitivity & environment count — post-call recap
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.k@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment pricing sensitivity & environment count — post-call recap

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few open items so we line up the proposal correctly: 

What we heard from MedLytics on the call:
- Use case: on-prem/VPC inference for clinical summarization and long-note retrieval (interactive API and background batch jobs).
- Initial rollout: 3 environments (dev, staging, prod), potential expansion to additional regions later.
- Expected token profile: 1.2B tokens/month initially (spiky daytime interactive + nightly batch), with tail growth to ~2B in 6–9 months.
- Required support: enterprise (24x7 with SLA + on-call escalation) and SOC2 evidence.
- Timeline: procurement evaluation in March, decision target end of Q2.

Open items for pricing: 
1) Licensing model preference: per-environment flat license vs. capacity-based (reserved GPU pools) — you said procurement prefers predictable monthly commitments but is open to a hybrid.
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target in the ballpark of $700 / 1M tokens (want to confirm a target band).
3) Environment counts & sizing: confirm whether the 3 envs are strictly separated by cluster or logically separated on shared capacity.
4) Procurement constraints: any required PO terms, minimum contract length, or security-specific addenda?

Next steps (suggested):
- I’ll put together two pricing paths: (A) 12-month private license per environment + Premium support, and (B) capacity-based committed GPUs with usage overlay.
- Marissa will prepare an initial commercial outline (list price + discount bands) to see whether we can hit target $ / 1M tokens.
- Neha will validate sizing assumptions (KV cache fit, batching expectations) and confirm whether KV caching can materially reduce token count for the interactive workload.

Attachments: please see the MedLytics input sheet I attached for your edits (MedLytics_Pricing_Input.xlsx).

If the summary looks right, confirm the target $/1M token range you want us to use when we build the spreadsheet.

Best,
Aditya
Aditya Rao | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
---
From: Sara Klein <sara.k@medlytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medlytics.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing sensitivity & environment count — post-call recap

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications and numbers from our side: 

- Token volumes: confirmed baseline 1.2B tokens/month with expected 1.8–2.0B by month 6 if initial tests go well. The interactive portion is the most sensitive to latency.
- Budget range: procurement has a guidance band of $55k–$90k / month for the first year (all-in, including support and licenses), but they're flexible if we can show strong unit economics vs hosted alternatives.
- Target $/1M tokens: medlytics would like to be around $600–$800 / 1M tokens (our finance prefers closer to $600, but they will accept up to $800 if justified by performance/SLA).
- Environment count: 3 environments for 12 months (dev/staging/prod). They prefer per-environment isolation (separate clusters) initially for compliance.
- Procurement timeline: procurement wants a commercial term sheet and SOC2 evidence by 3/24 so they can route to legal.

I attached our filled input sheet with expected Q1–Q4 token ramp and some procurement notes (Procurement contact is procurement@medlytics.com).

Can you share the two pricing paths you mentioned and a rough delta in list price between per-env vs capacity-committed pricing? We need ballpark numbers ASAP to justify to finance.

Thanks,
Sara Klein
Head of Product
MedLytics

On Wed, Mar 3, 2027 at 10:12 AM Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment pricing sensitivity & environment count — post-call recap

Marissa / Neha — forwarding the MedLytics recap and their clarified asks (see Sara’s reply). Action items I’m hoping we can move quickly on: 

1) Commercial ask (Marissa): build two ballpark price tables that map to their budget band and target unit econ:
   - Option A: Per-environment license (3 envs) + Premium support (24x7 SLA) — show list price and a 15–35% discount band.
   - Option B: Capacity-based committed GPUs (reserved pool) for all environments plus an overage/usage topping — show incremental unit $/1M tokens for baseline and scaled volumes.

   Please target a scenario where we can demonstrate hitting ~$700 / 1M tokens at an acceptable discount level. If that requires a minimum 12-month commit or a higher upfront fee, call it out (MedLytics mentioned procurement prefers predictable monthly commitments).

2) Technical ask (Neha): validate sizing for 1.2B -> 2.0B tokens/month. Key gating items:
   - KV cache effectiveness for interactive calls (how much token reduction realistic).
   - Whether their requirement for separate clusters (3 envs) forces us to price per-env vs. shared capacity.
   - Any limitations on model variants that would change GPU footprint or quantization options.

3) Docs: please attach the Redwood pricing worksheet and a draft SOW we can share with procurement. I started a draft pricing worksheet (attached: Redwood_Pricing_Worksheet_v1.xlsx).

Timing: Sara asked for commercial + SOC2 evidence by 3/24. Can we get first internal draft pricing + technical notes by EOD 3/5 so I can share an internal preview? 

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the external follow-up once we have a draft.

-Aditya

--- forwarded message ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing sensitivity & environment count — post-call recap

Perfect summary — I’ll take lead on the commercial and draft a proposal for the two paths. Quick notes from pricing perspective: 

- Base assumptions I’ll use: 1.2B tokens/month baseline, ramp to 1.8–2.0B in 6 months. 12-month term. 3 isolated environments (prod staged cluster sizing). Premium support (~10% uplift on license).
- Preliminary list estimate: per-environment license list ~$42k / env / month (list) — with Premium support this runs to ~$46k/env/month. That puts list near $138k/month for 3 envs (with support).
- To get to the MedLytics target ~$700 / 1M tokens at 1.2B tokens, we’d need an effective monthly spend of ~$840 (1.2B / 1M * $700 = $840k) — that’s not matching their budget band, so we need to cross-check math: looks like MedLytics numbers are for a different token accounting (they may be counting only user-facing tokens and not batch).
- Capacity-based committed GPUs: list profile looks ~ $210k/month list for baseline pools (before support) but with batching/KV caching can drop effective $/1M tokens materially — I’ll model a 20–40% reduction depending on caching.

Action plan: I’ll produce a short commercial memo + 2 pricing worksheets (Per-env license vs committed capacity) and include discount scenarios that land us in $600–$800 / 1M token range. I’ll flag whether that requires a minimum ARR or term.

Neha — can you confirm by EOD 3/5:
- a recommended cluster sizing for prod/staging/dev (GPU count & instance sizing)
- KV cache reduction estimate (conservative and optimistic)

I’ll attach a draft SOW and the pricing worksheet in the next email to share with Sara/procurement.

Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments included: Draft_SOW_MedLytics.pdf, Redwood_Pricing_Worksheet_v1.xlsx
